A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TerraMind work and provide readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and supplementary material. Content can be reliably matched despite layout changes.

before.justification: v2 reports original fusion, generation, few-shot, PANGAEA, and TiM experiments, with additional tokenizer and geolocation analyses in the appendix.

after.justification: v4 retains original experimental results in the main text and appendix, including benchmark evaluations, tokenizer analyses, and TiM crop-mapping results.

M1.justification: The FSQ/diffusion tokenizers, dual-scale Transformer encoder-decoder, Dirichlet masking, cross-entropy objective, generation procedures, and TiM augmentation remain the same. Shortened explanations and the corrected TiM recurrence notation do not establish a procedural change.

E1.justification: Both versions retain TerraMesh pretraining, the same nine PANGAEA datasets, EuroSAT and METER-ML few-shot evaluations, water and crop mapping, geolocation analyses, and Singapore/Spain generation examples. No dataset, task, or evaluated input scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Table 6 removes TerraMindv1-B-single as a PANGAEA comparator, although this variant remains evaluated elsewhere. External baseline membership in the performance comparisons is unchanged. DiffusionSat's removal from the architectural overview in Table 1 is not an empirical baseline removal.

E3.justification: Figure 1 changes the reported pretraining budget from 1 trillion to 500 billion tokens, matching the 500B-token setting already stated in both versions' scaling descriptions. This is a reported-setting correction; the PDFs do not establish retraining. Other retained experimental protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Removing the B-single row from Table 6 reduces the quantitative ablation evidence comparing single-scale and dual-scale pretraining across PANGAEA. The fusion, FSQ-versus-VQ, geographic-error, pseudo-label, tokenized-input, and TiM crop-mapping analyses remain.

E5.justification: Tables 5 and 11 retain mean accuracies averaged over 200 runs. Run-count disclosures and uncertainty-reporting practices are unchanged; neither version adds confidence intervals, significance tests, or seed information.

E6.justification: Table 6 loses seven B-single scores, including 84.00 on BurnScars and 40.80 on PASTIS; retained table values are unchanged. Section 5.3 corrects DeCUR's stated IoU from 84.4% to 82.2%, consistent with Table 4's unchanged 82.17, and correctly attributes the 45.4% zero-shot result to TerraMindv1-B.

T1.justification: v4 omits the explicit Dirichlet density and probability/weighting-parameter definitions from v2 Equation 1. The joint-distribution factorization in v2 Equation 4 is reduced to a verbal description. Cross-entropy, the random-loss expression, and the substantive TiM recursion remain; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The introduction changes its claimed benefit from the autoregressive paradigm to token-based pretraining. The abstract and contribution list foreground embedding-space structure in place of zero/few-shot capabilities. The central claims of any-to-any generation, TiM benefits, and benchmark superiority remain.

C2.justification: Supplementary Section 10.3 removes the expectation that TiM would further improve several PANGAEA tasks. Section 5.6 also drops the qualification that TiM strongly benefits from a trainable encoder. Existing interpretations and limitations concerning tokenizer artifacts, geolocation, and low-information generation remain.

D1.justification: The abstract adds explicit model and code access locations, and Figure 7 identifies B-single as the generating model. Conversely, Table 2 loses its explicit frozen-tokenizer-encoder description, and Section 7 removes the caption-release promise. Most implementation, hardware, and hyperparameter details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The bibliography retains the same 76 works. Positioning changes modestly through DiffusionSat's removal from Table 1, explicit attribution of caption generation to reference 47, and attribution of the two-stage training procedure to 4M.

P1.justification: The abstract is rewritten, explanations and captions are shortened, the TiM discussion and conclusion are condensed, and model names are standardized. Most paragraphs and the section order remain intact, while appendix prose changes little.

P2.justification: Figure 6 changes from four vertically stacked panels to a two-by-two arrangement, and Figure 4 corrects 'Finite State' to 'Finite Scalar' Quantization. The author block and float placement are compacted, captions are edited, and Tables 1 and 6 lose rows. Appendix visual content is retained.

improvement.justification: v4 improves consistency in the zero-shot discussion and pretraining caption and provides clearer resource access. However, removing the single-scale PANGAEA scores leaves the dual-scale-benefit assertion in supplementary Section 10.3 without its corresponding numerical comparison, including cases where B-single performed better. This loss of checkable evidence for a central design choice outweighs the limited editorial and documentation gains.
